vacuity_of_z3_reentry.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
vacuity_of_z3_reentry.statement: a weight-3 edge landing on an already-open orbit is ALWAYS classified R, never Z3, by joint_kind's own definition and extend()'s new_orbit=(om[q]==0) computation. 'Z3 re-entry' is not a distinct legal move category -- any edge matching that description is, by definition, an R, already proven unavailable (R-budget exhausted at R1+R2). Only Z2 and Z3-fresh-opening are real repair candidates.

Z2.component_partition: may merge the orbit's component with the target hexagon's component if the hexagon already has a vertex in a different component; otherwise extends the orbit's own component
Z2.hub_touch_count: +1 iff target hexagon is the hub (identical rule for both kinds; check is hexagon_id(target)==hub_id, independent of joint_kind)
Z2.F_def: +1 iff not state.visited(word_after(state.p, SIGMA)) -- a check on the PRE-edge position's own visited-set, referencing neither this edge's target, kind, nor the incidence forest
Z2.r1_target_ancestry: unaffected unless this edge's target hexagon already lies in R1-target's component
Z2.terminal_geometry_risk: F at risk only via the abandonment mechanism; H never at risk (dH=max(weight-3,0)=0 for weight<=3)

Z3.component_partition: attaches the new orbit's singleton to the target hexagon's existing component, or starts a fresh singleton if the hexagon has none yet
Z3.F_def: identical rule -- dF computation in extend() does not branch on joint_kind

causal_independence_hand_proof.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
causal_independence_hand_proof.claim: F_def's update rule is causally independent of the incidence-forest/component-merge mechanism
causal_independence_hand_proof.proof: dF is computed from state.visited(word_after(state.p, SIGMA)) alone -- a predicate over the OLD orbit's own rotation-continuation and the global visited-set, containing no reference to orbit_masks, incidence_components, or which hexagon the NEW edge targets. Whether an edge merges two components has no causal bearing on whether it triggers F_exceeded.

task_3_minimum_merge_conditions.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
conditions: 1. the repair's own orbit already belongs to (or, for Z3, becomes) one side of the pair -- the R2-source's eventual small component
2. its target hexagon already has a vertex in the OTHER side -- R1-target's component (spans 8 distinct hexagons per the one fully-detailed exported sample, not only the hub)
3. that target PERMUTATION (not merely the hexagon) has not already been visited, or exact_permutation_collision rejects the edge before the forest is consulted
task_3_minimum_merge_conditions.granularity_note: condition 3 is not automatically satisfied by condition 2: the union-find operates at HEXAGON granularity while collision is checked at PERMUTATION granularity. A hexagon with popcount<6 has a free slot a repair could target without colliding, even though that hexagon already has a vertex from some other, already-visited slot. Only a hexagon at popcount=6 (the hub is the one directly observed example) is collision-saturated for every possible target.

task_4_lemma_verdicts.statement: a Z2 repair cannot merge two distinct components
task_4_lemma_verdicts.argument: Z2's effect on the forest is mechanically identical to Z3's (one new orbit-vertex-to-hexagon-vertex edge) except it reuses an existing orbit-vertex. Nothing in Z2's definition constrains which hexagon its fixed move-formula target lands in relative to any existing component.
task_4_lemma_verdicts.counterpattern: any Z2 edge whose orbit q sits in component C_q, landing at a fresh phase whose target hexagon h already has a vertex in a different component C_h, merges C_q and C_h -- the generic case, not a special one

task_4_lemma_verdicts.statement: any Z3 repair that merges the needed components consumes the only remaining allowed hub touch
task_4_lemma_verdicts.argument: would only hold if the ONLY hexagon already in R1-target's component were the hub itself. It is not.
task_4_lemma_verdicts.counterpattern: R1-target's component has {e_orbits:2, hexagons:8, incidences:10} per the exported sample -- 8 distinct hexagons, hub only one of them. A Z3 opening a fresh orbit whose target lands in any of the other 7 already-in-component hexagons (popcount<6) merges the needed components without touching the hub at all.
task_4_lemma_verdicts.data_source: outputs/rr_short_ell0_v3_component_failures.json records[0], already exported, not newly inferred

task_4_lemma_verdicts.statement: any legal repair changes the future R2 source orbit
task_4_lemma_verdicts.argument: inserting any additional macro edge (Z2 or Z3, kind-agnostic) lengthens the walk's history by one edge, so every subsequent rotation-run's landing position shifts relative to the un-repaired walk, since a rotation-run's landing is a deterministic function of the exact preceding position. No repair type or placement leaves later R2 candidates' source orbit unchanged.
task_4_lemma_verdicts.generalizes: the prior round's proof, stated there only generically for 'the repair event'; confirmed here to hold for both concrete repair types (Z2 and Z3)

task_4_lemma_verdicts.statement: a repair preserving terminal geometry must occur before completer
task_4_lemma_verdicts.argument: F_def's update rule references only the pre-edge position's own rotation-continuation and the global visited-set -- no term for completer timing or macro_index. H is never at risk from any weight<=3 edge regardless of timing. Terminal-geometry preservation and completer timing are governed by disjoint state (F/H vs. Decoration.completer).
task_4_lemma_verdicts.counterpattern: abstract -- a Z3 edge fired strictly between R1 and the re-attempted R2 (hence necessarily after the historical completer in this lineage), targeting a non-hub, non-full hexagon already in R1-target's component; nothing established forces this to trigger an abandonment or exceed the hub-touch cap merely because it occurs after the completer

task_4_lemma_verdicts.statement: a repair after completer necessarily causes F_exceeded or collision
task_4_lemma_verdicts.grade: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF -- exhaustive empirical refutation, not merely abstract
task_4_lemma_verdicts.argument: in event 4's lineage the completer fires at macro_index 4, strictly before R1 (macro_index 5) -- so every one of the 100,245 post-R1 node expansions in this run is, by definition, 'after completer'.
task_4_lemma_verdicts.exhaustive_evidence: outputs/rr_short_ell0_v3_frontier_export.json's 85 frontier states report F:{1} exhaustively, zero exceptions -- not one of the tens of thousands of accepted, expanded edges in this post-completer region ever pushed F above 1
task_4_lemma_verdicts.caveat_stated_precisely: this exhausts ORDINARY post-completer continuations, not a repair-classified edge specifically (no confirmed successful repair exists anywhere in this data, Target_A_hits=0). The refutation rests on (a) the proven causal-independence argument (task_2), which applies regardless of whether an edge also merges components, plus (b) the exhaustive empirical absence of F_exceeded among all accepted post-completer edges -- not on a directly observed successful repair, which does not exist in this data

task_5_summary.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
task_5_summary.net_result: four of five candidate lemmas are false, and the one true lemma (C) does not by itself forbid a repair -- it only says a repair cannot be evaluated against the original 5,419 candidates, it produces new ones. No proven obstruction to a legal, component-merging, geometry-preserving repair was found this round, and none is fabricated. A genuinely permissive result relative to what the candidate lemmas, if true, would have implied.

task_6_smallest_repair_template.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL -- not a claim this template is realized in the data, not searched for
task_6_smallest_repair_template.edge_kind: Z3 (fresh orbit) preferred -- does not require the repair's own orbit to already be registered; a Z2 template is equally unruled-out if its orbit already sits in the eventual R2-source component (Lemma A)
task_6_smallest_repair_template.timing: strictly after R1, strictly before the re-attempted R2 candidate (necessarily 'after completer' in this lineage -- Lemma D shows this is not disqualifying)
task_6_smallest_repair_template.target_hexagon: any hexagon already possessing a forest vertex in R1-target's component, EXCLUDING the hub hexagon (Lemma B: 7 such non-hub hexagons already known to exist) AND excluding any hexagon already at popcount=6 (collision risk, task_3 condition 3)
task_6_smallest_repair_template.target_phase_slot: any of that hexagon's not-yet-visited permutations
task_6_smallest_repair_template.resulting_orbit: becomes the new orbit the repair's own vertex sits in; a later R2 candidate would need its own rotation-run to land back in THIS specific orbit for the repair to matter to it (Lemma C: this is a new, not-yet-characterized candidate, not one of the 5,419 already on record)
task_6_smallest_repair_template.required_check: F stays <=1 immediately after -- not guaranteed by any proof above (task_2's independence proof shows it is POSSIBLE to satisfy, not that it is impossible to fail); must be checked per concrete edge
